steps.name: Verify mTLS proxy
steps.run:
RESOLVE="${E2E_HOME_ASSISTANT_HOST}:8443:127.0.0.1"
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -s --cacert "$MTLS_DIR/ca.pem" --resolve "$RESOLVE" "$E2E_MTLS_URL/" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 1
done

# The manifest needs no authentication, so anything proxied would be a 200.
# Without the client certificate the proxy itself must answer 400.
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --cacert "$MTLS_DIR/ca.pem" --resolve "$RESOLVE" \
  "$E2E_MTLS_URL/manifest.json")
if [ "$STATUS" != "400" ]; then
  echo "::error::Expected 400 from the proxy without a client certificate, got $STATUS"
  exit 1
fi

# With it, Home Assistant must answer through the proxy.
curl -sSf --cacert "$MTLS_DIR/ca.pem" \
  --cert "$MTLS_DIR/client.pem" --key "$MTLS_DIR/client.key" \
  --resolve "$RESOLVE" \

steps.name: Wait for emulators
steps.run:
ADB="$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb"
EXPECTED=$(grep -c . devices.txt)

# Up to 3 minutes; a slower start would not leave enough of the 20m session for the flows.
for _ in $(seq 1 36); do
  SERIALS=$($ADB devices | awk 'NR > 1 && $2 == "device" { print $1 }')
  if [ "$(echo "$SERIALS" | grep -c .)" -eq "$EXPECTED" ]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
done

COUNT=$(echo "$SERIALS" | grep -c .)
if [ "$COUNT" -ne "$EXPECTED" ]; then
  echo "::error::Expected $EXPECTED emulators connected through adb, got $COUNT"
  $ADB devices
  exit 1
fi

# Bounded so a session dying mid-boot fails the step instead of hanging the job.
for SERIAL in $SERIALS; do
  BOOTED=""
  for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
    if [ "$($ADB -s "$SERIAL" shell getprop sys.boot_completed 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')" = "1" ]; then
      BOOTED=1
      break
    fi
    sleep 1
  done
  if [ -z "$BOOTED" ]; then
    echo "::error::Emulator $SERIAL did not finish booting"
    $ADB devices
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Two onboardings per device overflow the default logcat buffer, and the
# "Capture Android logs" step runs after both.
for SERIAL in $SERIALS; do
  $ADB -s "$SERIAL" logcat -G 32M
done

echo "serials=$(echo $SERIALS | xargs)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

steps.name: Check whether the inputs artifact is still available
steps.run:
# Expired artifacts stay in the listing with `expired: true` rather than
# disappearing, so this covers both expiry and a missing upload.
available=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/artifacts?name=emulator-wtf-inputs" \
  --jq '[.artifacts[] | select(.expired == false)] | length > 0')
echo "available=$available" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [ "$available" != "true" ]; then
  echo "::error title=Instrumentation tests skipped::The emulator.wtf inputs from $RUN_URL are no longer available. A maintainer needs to re-run all jobs of that workflow to rebuild them."
fi

steps.name: Create PR check (in progress)
steps.run:
# Identify this job by its runner, not by display name. GitHub does
# not expose the current job's database id directly (no GITHUB_JOB_ID,
# no /actions/jobs/current endpoint — confirmed against the REST API
# docs), and $GITHUB_JOB is the YAML key, not the id we need for the
# URL. The jobs API returns a `runner_name` field on every job, and
# the runner exports its name as $RUNNER_NAME, so matching the two
# uniquely identifies this job regardless of how many siblings exist.
# `env.RUNNER_NAME` is jq's safe way to read the env var (no shell
# interpolation of the value into the filter string).
JOB_ID=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
  --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.runner_name == env.RUNNER_NAME) | .id][0]' || true)
# Defence-in-depth: only use JOB_ID in a URL if it looks like an id.
# gh returns integers here, but validating keeps the URL safe even if
# GitHub's response format ever changes, and guards against the
# selector ever matching zero or multiple jobs.
if [[ "$JOB_ID" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  JOB_URL="$RUN_URL/job/$JOB_ID"
else
  JOB_URL="$RUN_URL"
fi
SUMMARY="Full logs: [open this emulator.wtf job →]($JOB_URL)"
check_id=$(jq -n \
    --arg sha "$HEAD_SHA" \
    --arg url "$JOB_URL" \
    --arg summary "$SUMMARY" \
    '{
       name: "Instrumentation Test app",
       head_sha: $sha,
       status: "in_progress",
       details_url: $url,
       output: {title: "Running on emulator.wtf", summary: $summary}
     }' \
  | gh api --method POST "repos/$REPO/check-runs" --input - --jq '.id')
{
  echo "check_id=$check_id"
  echo "job_url=$JOB_URL"
} >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

steps.name: Run zizmor
steps.run:
# Compiled gh-aw workflows (*.lock.yml) are generated by `gh aw compile`,
# so findings there cannot be fixed or suppressed in place. They are excluded.
# The exit code is deferred to the last step, so the SARIF is always produced.
git ls-files -z -- \
  '.github/workflows/*.yml' '.github/workflows/*.yaml' \
  '.github/actions/*/action.yml' '.github/actions/*/action.yaml' \
  '.github/dependabot.yml' '.github/dependabot.yaml' \
  ':!.github/workflows/*.lock.yml' \
  | xargs -0 uvx "zizmor==${ZIZMOR_VERSION}" \
    --pedantic --strict-collection --no-exit-codes \
    --no-progress --format=sarif > zizmor.sarif

steps.name: Report findings
steps.run:
jq -r '.runs[].results[] | "\(.level): \(.locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri):\(.locations[0].physicalLocation.region.startLine) [\(.ruleId)] \(.message.text)"' zizmor.sarif
count="$(jq '[.runs[].results[]] | length' zizmor.sarif)"
if [[ "${count}" -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "::error::zizmor reported ${count} finding(s), listed above and in the Security tab under Code scanning. Fix them, or add an inline 'zizmor: ignore' comment with a reason."
  exit 1
fi
echo "No findings."

steps.name: Open or comment on the zizmor-failure issue
steps.run:
# Empty when the label does not exist yet, i.e. nothing ever failed.
NUMBER=$(gh issue list --label zizmor-failure --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number' || true)
if [ -n "$NUMBER" ]; then
  gh issue comment "$NUMBER" --body "The weekly zizmor scan failed again in $RUN_URL."
else
  gh issue create --label zizmor-failure \
    --title "Weekly zizmor scan of the GitHub Actions workflows failed" \
    --body "The scheduled zizmor scan on main failed: $RUN_URL. Review the findings in the run log or under Security > Code scanning."
fi
